S. and Byron had discussed the poem at the meeting, which prompted the poem: ‘We talked of literary
matters, his fourth Canto which he says is very good, & indeed repeated some stanzas of great energy
to me’ (L ii 37). Julian is answering Maddalo with Maddalo’s (Byron’s) own opinions, and this fits, per-
haps, with S.’s desire at the time that Byron should live up to his professed ideals. See headnote.
